newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian Justice Minister said ready to resign.
newsitem.headline: Colombian Justice Minister said ready to resign.

text.p: Justice Minister Carlos Medellin, a leading proponent of lifting Colombia's constitutional ban on extradition, is preparing to resign, government sources said on Wednesday.

Medellin, who has won high marks from Washington for his role in pushing tough anti-drug laws through Congress since he took office early last year, will step down within the next two weeks, the government sources said.
"The minister has decided to resign, the decision is already taken and in about two weeks he'll formalise it with his letter in writing," an official at the Justice Ministry said.

He added that Medellin was leaving the government to launch a possible bid for a congressional seat or to stand as the running- mate of presidential hopeful Carlos Lleras de la Fuente in elections next year.

At the urging of Medellin, and acting under intense pressure from the United States, President Ernesto Samper announced just last week that he would put forward legislation that would lift the ban on extradition of drug lords and other criminals introduced by Colombia's constituyent assembly in 1991.
U.S. officials have said repeatedly that detention in a secure facility in the United States is what Colombia's powerful drug lords fear the most.
